fig4.title: Fig. 4. Transient thermal impedance from junction to mounting base as a function of pulse duration (page 5)
fig4.curve: the lowest curve, labelled duty cycle 0.01 (the figure prints no single-pulse curve; a duty-cycle curve lies above the single pulse, so reading it bounds a single pulse from above)
fig4.method: page 5 rendered at 400 dpi in grey (pdftoppm -r 400 -gray); the axes located on the rendered page by the printed grid: the decade lines 1e-5 s at x 519.5 px and 1 s at x 2786 px (453.3 px a decade), 10 K/W at y 1126.4 px and 0.01 K/W at y 2014.4 px (296 px a decade, the minor lines 9 to 2 at the expected log offsets); at each pulse width the centre of the lowest dark run at least 4 px thick, a column clear of the vertical grid; one pixel is 0.0078 of a decade in Z (1.8 percent)
fig4.note: the curve's plateau (1.3225 K/W) lies between Table 6's Rth(j-mb) typical 1.1 and maximum 1.4 K/W; the record scales the curve so that its plateau is the maximum 1.4 K/W

fig12.title: Fig. 12. Input, output and reverse transfer capacitances as a function of drain-source voltage; typical values (page 8)
fig12.method: page 8 rendered at 150 dpi, the decade lines 100 pF and 1000 pF located on the page (164 px a decade); the Ciss curve read at the left end of the axis
fig12.note: typical values only; the sheet prints no maximum Ciss and no variation; the curve rises as |VDS| falls
